topics.topic: Atomicity and persistence of outputs, external effects, and model mutations from an unrecorded execution
questions: What does `it has no effect` refer to, and are outputs or external effects from the recordless execution guaranteed absent, rolled back, ignored, or potentially still present when recovery re-executes the function?

What exactly has no effect: the unrecorded execution, the recovery execution, or only the failed trace-record write; and must every output StoredValue, spooled file, resource fact, and other state produced by the unrecorded execution be absent?
What does “it has no effect” mean: that the first function execution has no domain or external effects, that recovery has no additional effect, or only that no trace record is stored?

Does “leaves none” mean only that no NodeExecution record remains, or that every model change produced by that execution—including Run outputs or status, StoredValues, and SpooledFiles—is absent or rolled back?

quotes:
An element that does not
      succeed keeps no output: its NodeExecution names none, a value it produced
   is not stored, and the files its attempt spooled are discarded: no
   SpooledFile record names them and nothing reads them.

Their bytes are
   removed at once only by a spool-ceiling refusal (A15 rule 3); after any
   other failure they stay in the run's spool, counted toward
   `spool_run_bytes_max`, until that spool is removed (A18 rule 4) or a later
   write to the same position replaces them — a position being the run, node,
   `map_index`, attempt number, port and list index, which only a retry of
   the same attempt number writes again, after a restart left that attempt
   without a record. Value bytes it published stay in the content-addressed area
   unnamed, reused by equal bytes until the next start removes them (A18 rule
   4); nothing reads either.

function element without a
   concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect;
judgement.why: State 2 specifies that unrecorded output records are absent, any residual bytes are unreadable and cleaned or replaced, and re-execution is safe because a function has no effect.

topics.topic: Run and WaitingPoint lifecycle state between trace-record refusal and recovery
questions: What Run status applies after the kernel stops on a refused trace write and before recovery, and which transition enters and leaves that condition?
What status does the existing Run have between the refused record and recovery?
What status does the Run have between the store refusal and recovery, and does it acquire a WaitingPoint with an existing reason or remain `running` without one?

quotes:
On start, before the surface accepts a request, the kernel turns every
   `in_flight` EffectAttempt into `unknown` (A11 rule 4) and then derives every
   run that has not ended — `running`, `awaiting_approval` or `pending` — again
   from its records, oldest first in store order, rewriting a stored status or
   waiting point that lags them (a decided approval, a resolved attempt, an
   outcome whose run change was lost), and advances, as the
   kernel actor, every run that derivation leaves `running`: a
   function element without a
   concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it has no effect;
judgement.why: State 2 makes startup recovery derive the existing Run's status and WaitingPoints from durable records and automatically advance it when that derivation is running.

topics.topic: Whether a refused function trace record creates any NodeExecution, transiently or persistently
questions: When the store refuses a function execution's record, is that execution an exception that creates no NodeExecution, or must every node execution still create one?
Does a concluded function execution for which the store refuses the trace record create a NodeExecution, given K-09 says that it leaves none?
Was a NodeExecution value created transiently and then discarded, or does a NodeExecution come into existence only when the store accepts its immutable record?

quotes:
Every node execution writes one immutable trace record: run, node, pinned
versions, input and output by digest, verdicts, status, failure, resources, time.

A
function execution during which the kernel stops because the store refused its
record leaves none, and recovery executes the function again: it has no effect.
judgement.why: The universal requirement that every node execution writes a record conflicts with the newly added exception saying a concluded function execution leaves none.

basis:
Every node execution writes one immutable trace record: run, node, pinned
versions, input and output by digest, verdicts, status, failure, resources, time. A
function execution during which the kernel stops because the store refused its
record leaves none, and recovery executes the function again: it has no effect.

The trace record of one concluded attempt at one node, or of a node that was not
executed because its guards disabled it or an upstream node failed (K-09). Read by the owner
and agents reading traces, by repair (K-12) and by capture into a trial corpus.

topics.topic: Whether an unrecorded execution consumes an attempt_number
questions: Does the recordless execution consume an attempt_number, making the recovery execution a new attempt, or does recovery reuse the same attempt_number because no NodeExecution was minted?
Does the unrecorded function execution count when deriving the `attempt_number` of the record produced by its recovery execution?

Does the unrecorded function execution consume an `attempt_number`, so that the recovered execution's NodeExecution uses the next number, or does recovery reuse the same number because no record exists?

quotes:
For one run, node and element, `attempt_number` is the ordinal of the
   element's NodeExecution M23 records: each NodeExecution written for the
   element takes the next number, from 1, whatever its status — an execution, a
   send, a pre-send failure, an owner's refusal, a skip, an upstream failure, the
   record of a mapped node over an empty list.

Nothing
   else takes or holds a number: waiting for approval writes no NodeExecution,
   and the owner's resolution of an unknown outcome writes no NodeExecution
   names (A18 rules 1, 2, 4).
judgement.why: State 2 defines attempt_number solely as the ordinal of durable NodeExecution records, so a recordless execution consumes no number.

quotes:
then the request is made; then one store call writes the outcome: the
   EffectAttempt's conclusion, the next NodeExecution, the values it produced,
   and the approval it used marked `used` — unless the attempt ended `not_sent`,
   which leaves it `approved` (M24). A crash between those two calls is the
   `in_flight` case of rule 4, whose recovery also marks that approval `used`.

On start, every EffectAttempt still `in_flight`, oldest first in store
   order and one store call per attempt, becomes `unknown`; when its
   attempt has no NodeExecution yet, the kernel writes it with status
   `outcome_unknown`, the binding as what it executed, the inputs the
   EffectAttempt names, no outputs, its start time taken from the EffectAttempt and its end
   time the time of recovery, and, when the attempt's authority is an approval,
   marks that approval `used`, in the same store call, one call per attempt. The element
   waits as in rule 2; the kernel does not ask the service.
judgement.why: State 2 records an effect attempt before sending and turns an incomplete in-flight operation into outcome_unknown on startup without sending it again.

topics.topic: Whether the existing Run and its identity, inputs, implementations, and state continue across recovery
questions: Does the Run retain the same `run_id`, pinned implementations, inputs and accumulated state when the kernel stops on a refused trace record and recovery executes the function again?

quotes:
Continuity: the run stays the same while
it advances, waits and ends.

One execution of one active flow version (K-09). Read by the executor as it
advances, by the owner and agents inspecting it, and by resume and cancel.
judgement.why: M19 expressly preserves the Run's identity throughout advancement and waiting, while its version, implementations and inputs are pinned at start.
